Installing cmdstanr on Windows

Jordan Hart, Joe Wilde

Source: vignettes/windows_installation.Rmd
windows_installation.Rmd

bisonR fits models with Stan, through the cmdstanr package and the CmdStan program. Installing these on Windows can be more involved than on other systems, particularly on managed or networked computers. This article lists problems we have encountered and solutions that have worked. The general installation instructions are in the cmdstanr documentation.

Before installing

CmdStan compiles models with a C++ toolchain, which on Windows is provided by Rtools. Install the version of Rtools that matches your version of R, then install cmdstanr and check the toolchain:

install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::check_cmdstan_toolchain(fix = TRUE)
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()

Installing on a networked computer

On computers in universities and other organisations, the HOME directory is often on a network drive. Installing CmdStan there can fail (for example, with errors from tar.exe), or be very slow. Instead, create a folder on a local drive that isn’t synchronised with the network, and install CmdStan there:

cmdstanr::install_cmdstan(dir = "C:/path/to/local/folder")

cmdstanr may not find this installation in later sessions. If so, set its location at the start of each session (or in your .Rprofile), pointing to the folder for the installed version:

cmdstanr::set_cmdstan_path("C:/path/to/local/folder/cmdstan-2.36.0")

“Rtools was not found but is required to run CmdStan”

This happens when the environment variable that tells R where Rtools is installed hasn’t been set. Check that the installed version of Rtools matches your version of R. If it does, set the variable for your version of Rtools (for example RTOOLS44_HOME for Rtools 4.4, or RTOOLS45_HOME for Rtools 4.5) to the folder where Rtools is installed, then restart R.

“Supplied CSV file is corrupt”

This error appears after sampling. We have not identified its cause, but updating cmdstanr to the latest version has fixed it for us:

install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))

If the error continues, update R to the latest release.

“CmdStan path has not been set yet”

This can happen in a new R session after CmdStan has been installed, usually on managed computers that do not keep the CMDSTAN environment variable set during installation. Set the path with cmdstanr::set_cmdstan_path() as shown above, or set the CMDSTAN environment variable to the folder for the installed version (for example C:/Users/you/.cmdstan/cmdstan-2.36.0), rather than to the .cmdstan folder that contains it.

Other problems

If none of these solutions work, please ask in Discussions, including the error message and your versions of R, Rtools and cmdstanr. Reports of solutions that work on other systems are also welcome.
